mainTopic: Why a גט cannot serve as a כתובה document, and when found documents such as גיטין may be returned
overview: The amud opens by finishing the question of why אביי took back his challenge to רבי יוחנן. רבי יוחנן holds that a woman with only a גט still collects her כתובה. The גמרא first rejects two outside sources, the betrothed-widow משנה and the ברייתא of רב חייא בר אמי, because each could be about a written כתובה. The real reason comes from our משנה itself. A גט never mentions the 100 or 200 דינרים, and even if it counted as written, the husband could claim he already paid. Tearing the גט or writing a note on its back does not fix this, since not every payment happens in a בית דין. Next, a new משנה rules that found documents such as גיטין, release documents of slaves, wills, gift documents and receipts are not returned, because the writer may have changed his mind. The גמרא infers that if the writer says 'give', we return them even after a long time. That seems to contradict a משנה in גיטין, and רבה answers that it depends on whether caravans pass through often. The גמרא then limits the worry about a second person with the same name to cases where such a person is known to live in the city. To prove this, it begins a story about a גט found in רב הונא's בית דין, and that story continues on the next amud.

steps.title: 'Collects everything' must mean a written כתובה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the proof from the משנה of the betrothed widow. The phrase 'she collects everything' only makes sense if a כתובה was actually written for her.
steps.simpleTranslation: What does 'she collects everything' mean? If there were no written כתובה, all she would have is the basic 100 or 200 דינרים!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is knocking down a suggested reason for אביי's retraction. It shows that the משנה about an אלמנה מן האירוסין is talking about a woman who had a written כתובה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If no כתובה were written, the woman would only get the fixed basic sum (מנה or מאתים) that the חכמים guarantee every wife. The word 'everything' points to extra amounts the husband added, and those exist only in a written document. So this משנה proves nothing about a woman collecting with no document.

keyTerms.meaning: She collects everything, meaning the full amount owed to her
100 דינרים, the basic כתובה of a widow or non-virgin
200 דינרים, the basic כתובה of a בתולה
That she has, meaning what she is entitled to

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the גמרא is saying a betrothed widow gets nothing. The point is only that this משנה must be talking about a written כתובה, so it cannot be the source for collecting without one.

phrases.english: What is meant by 'she collects everything'?
All she has is the one hundred or two hundred!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the discussion from before this section, where the משנה of the betrothed widow was offered as the reason אביי retracted.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the משנה of אלמנה מן האירוסין as the reason for אביי's retraction.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: 'Collects everything' only fits a case with a written כתובה, so the משנה says nothing about a place where no כתובה is written.

steps.title: Trying the ברייתא of רב חייא בר אמי instead
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests a different source: a ברייתא that says a betrothed woman collects her כתובה if her husband dies.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, maybe the source is what רב חייא בר אמי taught. A man does not mourn for his betrothed wife and does not become טמא for her, and she does not mourn for him or become טמא for him. If she dies, he does not inherit her. If he dies, she collects her כתובה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא offers a new source to explain why אביי took back his challenge. It brings a ברייתא that seems to show a betrothed woman collects a כתובה even without a written one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An ארוסה usually has no written כתובה yet, because that is normally written at the נישואין. So if the ברייתא says she collects her כתובה, it seems a woman can collect her כתובה with no document at all. That would back רבי יוחנן's view that a woman holding only a גט still collects, because her right comes from the חכמים and not from a document. It would also explain why אביי dropped his idea that the גט serves as her כתובה.

keyTerms.meaning: A woman who is betrothed (after קידושין, before נישואין)
Has the status of an אונן, the intense mourning before the burial of a close relative
Becomes ritually impure, as a כהן may do for close relatives
Inherits her
Her כתובה payment

phrases.aramaic: וְאֶלָּא, מִדְּתָנֵי רַב חִיָּיא בַּר אַמֵּי:
phrases.english: Rather, from what Rav Ḥiyya bar Ami taught:
His betrothed wife:
he does not enter acute mourning, and does not become impure for her,
phrases.notes: Becoming impure here means a כהן going to her funeral, which he may only do for close relatives.

phrases.english: and likewise she does not enter acute mourning
and does not become impure for him.
If she dies, he does not inherit her;
if he dies, she collects her marriage contract.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאֶלָּא, מִדְּתָנֵי רַב חִיָּיא בַּר אַמֵּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the first source was rejected, a second source is offered.
steps.raayaObject: That a woman collects her כתובה even when no כתובה was written, which would explain אביי's retraction.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא of רב חייא בר אמי: if a betrothed woman's husband dies, she collects her כתובה.

steps.title: Maybe he wrote her a כתובה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the proof: the ברייתא could be talking about a case where the husband already wrote a כתובה during אירוסין.
steps.simpleTranslation: Perhaps he wrote her a כתובה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the new proof. The ברייתא may be about a betrothed woman who already had a written כתובה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Sometimes a man writes the כתובה already at אירוסין. If that is the case in the ברייתא, she collects because of the document, and nothing is proven about collecting without one.

keyTerms.meaning: Perhaps, a word used to suggest another way to read the source
That he wrote her a כתובה

phrases.english: Perhaps it is where he wrote her a marriage contract.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof offered in step 2.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the ברייתא of רב חייא בר אמי as proof.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The ברייתא can be read as a case where a כתובה was written, so it shows nothing about a case with no document.

steps.title: Then why state the obvious?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא raises a problem with the rejection: if a כתובה was written, it is obvious she collects, so why would the ברייתא need to say it?
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you will say: if he wrote her a כתובה, why say it at all?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the rejection it just made. If there was a written כתובה, of course she collects, so the ברייתא would be teaching nothing new.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A ברייתא is not supposed to state something obvious. If it is about a written כתובה, the line 'she collects her כתובה' looks pointless, and that would push us back to reading it as a case with no document.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you will say, which raises a possible objection
Why say it? This asks why something obvious is being stated

phrases.english: And if you will say: if he wrote her a marriage contract,
what is the point of stating it?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי תֵּימָא: דִּכְתַב לַהּ, מַאי לְמֵימְרָא
steps.kashyaTarget: The reading that the ברייתא is about a written כתובה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If a כתובה was written, her collecting it is obvious, so the ברייתא would be stating something with no new point.

steps.title: The new point is that he does not inherit her
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers: the main point of the ברייתא is the opposite case. If she dies, he does not inherit her. The line about her collecting was added only to balance it.
steps.simpleTranslation: It needed to teach: if she dies, he does not inherit her.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends the rejection. The real new teaching of the ברייתא is that a man does not inherit his betrothed wife, so the obvious line about her כתובה does no harm.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A husband inherits his wife only after נישואין, and the ברייתא needed to tell us that an ארוס does not. The line 'he dies, she collects her כתובה' was just said alongside it. So the ברייתא can still be about a written כתובה, and it gives no proof for אביי's retraction.

keyTerms.meaning: It was necessary for him, meaning this is the real new point being taught

phrases.english: 'If she dies, he does not inherit her'
was what he needed to teach.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 4 and confirms the rejection in step 3.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Shifts which part of the ברייתא carries the new teaching.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The line 'she collects her כתובה' must be teaching something new, so it must be about a case with no written כתובה.
steps.terutzMaskana: The new teaching is 'he does not inherit her'. The כתובה line can refer to a written כתובה, so the ברייתא proves nothing.

steps.title: אביי retracted because of the משנה itself
steps.stepSummary: The real reason for אביי's retraction comes from our משנה itself. A גט does not mention the 100 or 200 דינרים of a כתובה, so it cannot work as a כתובה document.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, אביי took back his challenge because of our משנה itself. If you think we are dealing with a place where people do not write a כתובה, so the גט acts as her כתובה, that does not work. Is 100 or 200 written in a גט?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives its final answer for why אביי took back his challenge. The reason comes from inside our משנה, not from outside sources.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי's idea was that in places without a written כתובה, the woman shows her גט to collect. But a גט says nothing about money and never mentions מנה or מאתים. So it is hard to call the גט her 'כתובה document', and אביי's suggested case does not fit the משנה.

keyTerms.meaning: Retracted, took back what he had said
From the משנה itself
If it enters your mind, meaning if you were to think
Is it then...? This asks a question that expects the answer 'no'
A bill of divorce

steps.whatToRemember: Two outside sources (the betrothed-widow משנה and רב חייא בר אמי's ברייתא) were each pushed off, because they could be about a written כתובה. אביי's real reason for retracting is that a גט never mentions the 100 or 200, so it cannot serve as a כתובה document.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows how the גמרא tests possible sources one by one, and drops each one that can be read another way, until it finds a reason that truly holds up.

phrases.english: Rather, from the משנה itself, Abaye
retracted,
because if it enters your mind
that we are dealing with a place where they do not write a marriage contract,
where the bill of divorce is her marriage contract,

phrases.aramaic: אַטּוּ גֵּט מָנֶה מָאתַיִם כְּתִיב בֵּיהּ?
phrases.english: is one hundred or two hundred written in a bill of divorce?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אַבָּיֵי מִגּוּפַהּ דְּמַתְנִיתִין קָא הָדַר בֵּיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After both outside sources were rejected, the גמרא goes back to the original question and answers it from the משנה itself.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: אביי retracted because a גט does not record the מנה or מאתים, so it cannot serve as a כתובה document. This means his suggested case does not fit the משנה.

steps.title: Even if the amount counts as written, the husband could claim he paid
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא considers a defense: since רבנן enacted that she collects with the גט, maybe it counts as if the amount were written in it. It rejects this, because the husband could still claim he already paid.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you would say: since the רבנן enacted that she collects with it, it is as if the amount is written in it. Still, the husband should be able to claim: I already paid.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא suggests a way to save the idea that a גט works like a כתובה, and right away shows a problem with it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 6 said a גט does not mention the 100 or 200 דינרים. The new suggestion is that the תקנה of רבנן makes it count as if the amount were written. But even then, a document she keeps after collecting cannot stop the husband from claiming he already paid, so the גט still fails as proof of an unpaid debt.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you would say: the גמרא brings up a possible defense
The רבנן enacted (made a rule)
It is as if it were written in it
I paid (a claim that the debt was already paid)

phrases.english: And if you would say:
since the Rabbis enacted
to collect with it,
phrases.notes: Some versions say לַהּ (for her) and some say בֵּיהּ (with it). The square-bracket wording is the corrected one.

phrases.english: it is as if it is written in it,
phrases.notes: He means the 100 or 200 דינרים of the כתובה, which step 6 said the גט leaves out.

phrases.english: let him claim and say: I paid.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Blocks a possible way around the reasoning of step 6
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the idea that the תקנה turns the גט into a complete כתובה document
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: A גט that stays with the woman cannot rule out the husband's claim that he already paid

steps.title: He could say she would not let him tear it
steps.stepSummary: Suppose we tell the husband that if he paid, he should have torn the גט. He can answer that she refused, because she needs the גט to remarry.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you would say we tell him: if you paid her, you should have torn it up. He can answer: she didn't let me, she said, I need it to remarry.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries to block the husband's claim of 'I paid' and shows that this attempt also fails.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally a paid debt document gets torn up, so a document that still exists suggests the debt is unpaid. A גט is different: the woman needs it as proof that she is divorced so she can marry again. So the husband has a good excuse for not tearing it.

keyTerms.meaning: To tear it up (done to a paid debt document)
She did not let me
To get married

phrases.english: And if you would say that we tell him:
If you paid her,
you should have torn it up,
he can tell us: She did not let me,
she said: I need it to remarry with it.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי תֵּימָא דְּאָמְרִינַן לֵיהּ: אִי פְּרַעְתַּהּ אִיבְּעִי לָךְ לְמִיקְרְעֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tries to block the 'I paid' claim from step 7, and fails
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the argument that the גט still existing proves the money was not paid
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: She has a real need to keep the גט, so it not being torn proves nothing

steps.title: Writing a note on the torn גט does not help, since not all collection is in court
steps.stepSummary: Suppose we say he should have torn the גט and written on its back why it was torn. That only works in a בית דין, and not every collection happens in a בית דין. So the גט cannot serve as a כתובה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you would say we tell him: you should have torn it and written on its back, 'We tore this גט not because it is invalid, but so she won't collect with it again.' Does everyone who pays out do it in a בית דין?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries one last fix, a note written on the torn גט, and rejects it. This completes the proof that a גט cannot work as a כתובה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A note on the back would let the woman keep a usable גט to remarry, while marking the כתובה as paid. But that kind of formal note is written by a בית דין, and many payments happen privately. So the husband's claim of 'I paid' still cannot be blocked, and the גט cannot be what she collects with.

keyTerms.meaning: On its back (the back of the document)
An invalid גט
Is it so that...? (introduces a question that pushes back)
A court (בית דין)

steps.whatToRemember: A גט cannot work as a כתובה document. It does not state the amount, and even if it did, the husband could claim he paid, since the woman keeps the גט and not every payment goes through a בית דין.

phrases.english: And if you would say we tell him:
You should have torn it
and written on its back:
This גט, that we tore it
is not because it is an invalid גט,
but rather so that
she should not collect with it another time.

phrases.aramaic: אַטּוּ כֹּל דְּמַגְבֵּי, בְּבֵי דִינָא מַגְבֵּי?
phrases.english: Is it so that everyone who pays out does it in court?

steps.triggerLanguage: אַטּוּ כֹּל דְּמַגְבֵּי, בְּבֵי דִינָא מַגְבֵּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the last attempt to block the husband's claim and closes the argument
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the fix of writing a note on the torn גט
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The fix needs a בית דין, but many payments are made privately
steps.whyThisMatters: This finishes the support for step 6. When a woman collects without a written כתובה, it cannot be because the גט acts as her document.

steps.title: New משנה: found documents that should not be returned
steps.stepSummary: The משנה rules that someone who finds a גט, a slave's release document, a will, a gift document, or a receipt should not return it. The writer may have decided not to deliver it.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: If someone found women's גיטין, slaves' release documents, wills, gift documents, or receipts, he should not return them. For I say: they were written, and the writer changed his mind and decided not to give them.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins with a new rule about lost documents.
steps.deeperAnalysis: These documents only take effect when they are handed over. Finding one does not prove it was ever delivered. Returning it could make it work when the writer may have decided against it.

keyTerms.meaning: Our משנה (marks the start of a משנה)
Documents that free slaves
Wills (documents for giving away property, usually by someone sick)
Receipts showing a debt was paid
He changed his mind

phrases.english: MISHNA: If one found women's bills of divorce
and slaves' freedom documents,
wills, gift documents, and receipts,
he should not return them.
For I say: they were written,
and he changed his mind about them, not to give them.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִי׳ מָצָא גִּיטֵּי נָשִׁים וְשִׁחְרוּרֵי עֲבָדִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic after the discussion of the גט and כתובה ends
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Someone who finds a גט, a slave's release document, a will, a gift document, or a receipt should not return it, because the writer may have decided not to deliver it.

steps.title: Inference from the משנה: if the writer says 'give,' we return it even after a long time
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא infers from our משנה that the only problem is that the writer may have changed his mind. If he says 'give it,' the finder returns the document even after a long time.
steps.simpleTranslation: The reason is that he may have decided not to give them. But if he said 'Give,' they give it, even after a long time.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens its discussion of the משנה by drawing an inference from it. This inference sets up the contradiction that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה gave only one reason not to return these documents: the writer may have decided not to deliver them. So if the writer confirms he wants it delivered, that worry is gone. Because the משנה sets no time limit, the גמרא assumes we return it even after a long time. That means we do not worry that the found document belongs to a different person with the same name.

keyTerms.meaning: The reason
He changed his mind / reconsidered
'Give!' (the writer tells us to deliver it)
After a long time

steps.confusionAlert: The words 'even after a long time' do not appear in the משנה. The גמרא reads them in because the משנה sets no time limit.

phrases.english: Gemara:
The reason is that he reconsidered and decided not to give them,
phrases.notes: 'He' is the person who wrote the document, as at the end of the משנה in step 10.

phrases.english: but if he said 'Give,' they give it,
and even after a long time.

steps.triggerLanguage: טַעְמָא דְּנִמְלַךְ שֶׁלֹּא לִתְּנָן, הָא אָמַר: ״תְּנוּ״ – נוֹתְנִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws an inference from the משנה quoted in step 10.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: If the writer says 'give,' the found document is returned, even after a long time. We do not worry about another person with the same name.

steps.title: Contradiction from the משנה in Gittin about a lost גט
steps.stepSummary: A משנה in גיטין says that if a messenger loses a גט, it is valid only if he finds it right away. If time has passed, it is invalid.
steps.simpleTranslation: And contrast this: someone bringing a גט who lost it. If he found it right away, it is valid. If not, it is invalid.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the inference from step 11 by quoting a משנה that seems to say the opposite.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In גיטין, a גט found after time has passed is invalid. The worry there is that it may be a different גט with the same names. But our משנה, as read in step 11, says we return a found document even after a long time and do not have that worry. The two משניות seem to clash.

keyTerms.meaning: 'And contrast them': the גמרא sets two sources against each other
The messenger bringing a גט to the woman
Immediately, right away
Valid / invalid

phrases.english: And contrast it with this:
phrases.notes: This is a משנה in גיטין 27a.

phrases.english: One who was bringing a bill of divorce, and it got lost from him:
if he found it immediately, it is valid;
if not, it is invalid.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the inference made in step 11.
steps.kashyaTarget: The inference that a found document is returned even after a long time.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה in גיטין worries that a document found later may belong to someone with the same names. That contradicts our משנה's apparent lack of that worry.

steps.title: רבה: the answer depends on whether caravans pass through
steps.stepSummary: רבה says the two משניות are not in conflict. The משנה in גיטין speaks of a place where caravans often pass. Our משנה speaks of a place where they rarely do.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה said: It is not difficult. Here it is a place where caravans are common. Here it is a place where caravans are not common.
steps.whatsHappening: רבה answers the contradiction by placing each משנה in a different kind of location.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Where many travelers pass through, another person with the same name could easily have dropped a similar document. So after time passes, we cannot be sure the found document is the same one. Where few travelers pass, that chance is very small, so the document can be returned even after a long time.

keyTerms.meaning: It is not difficult; the contradiction is resolved
Caravans, groups of travelers
Common, frequently found
'Here... here': each source is about a different case

steps.whatToRemember: The worry about another person with the same name depends on how many strangers pass through the place.

phrases.english: Rabba said: It is not difficult:
here, it is in a place where caravans are common,
phrases.notes: This first 'here' is the משנה in גיטין, where the found גט is invalid.

phrases.english: here, it is in a place where caravans are not common.
phrases.notes: This second 'here' is our משנה, where the document is returned.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the contradiction raised in step 12.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases (אוקימתא): each source refers to a different location.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The two משניות seemed to disagree about whether we worry about a same-name document.
steps.terutzMaskana: They agree. The worry exists only where caravans are common, and our משנה is about a place where they are not.

steps.title: Even where caravans are common, the worry applies only if two people share the name in one city
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא narrows the worry further. Even where caravans pass often, we worry only if it is known that two men named יוסף בן שמעון live in one city.
steps.simpleTranslation: And even in a place where caravans are common, the worry applies only where it is established that there are two men named יוסף בן שמעון in one city.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds a limit to רבה's answer. It explains exactly when the same-name worry applies.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Many caravans alone are not enough to make us suspicious. We worry only if it is known that two people with the exact same name live in the same city. This makes the case where a found גט becomes invalid even narrower.

keyTerms.meaning: It was established or known as fact
A sample name, standing for any two people with an identical name
One city

steps.confusionAlert: יוסף בן שמעון is just an example name, not a specific person.

phrases.english: And even in a place where caravans are common,

phrases.aramaic: וְהוּא שֶׁהוּחְזְקוּ שְׁנֵי יוֹסֵף בֶּן שִׁמְעוֹן בְּעִיר אַחַת.
phrases.english: it is only where it was established that there are two Yosef ben Shimons in one city.

steps.triggerLanguage: וַאֲפִילּוּ בִּמְקוֹם שֶׁהַשְּׁיָירוֹת מְצוּיוֹת – וְהוּא שֶׁהוּחְזְקוּ
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The same-name worry applies only where caravans are common and two people with the identical name are known to live in one city.

steps.title: Otherwise רבה would contradict himself
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא supports the rule from Step 14 by showing that without it, רבה would contradict himself.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because if you do not say this, then one statement of רבה contradicts another statement of רבה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is backing up the rule from Step 14: we worry only when two people with the same name are known to live in one city. It sets up the next move by warning that without this rule, רבה contradicts himself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In Step 13, רבה explained that where caravans pass often, a found גט might belong to someone else. If that worry applied whenever caravans are common, even with no known second person of the same name, it would clash with another ruling of רבה. Reading רבה's worry as limited to cases where two people with the same name are known to live in one city lets both rulings fit together.

keyTerms.meaning: Because if you do not say so. This is a way of proving a point by showing the problem you would face without it.
There is a difficulty: רבה contradicts רבה. This means two statements by the same חכם seem to clash.

phrases.english: For if you do not say so,
there is a difficulty between Rabba and Rabba.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּאִי לָא תֵּימָא הָכִי קַשְׁיָא דְּרַבָּה אַדְּרַבָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the limitation stated in Step 14 by showing that rejecting it would make רבה contradict himself.
steps.raayaObject: The rule that we worry about a second person only when it is known that two people with the same name live in one city.
steps.raayaSupportSource: Fitting together two statements of רבה, which would otherwise contradict each other.

steps.title: A divorce document found in רב הונא's court
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins a story about a גט found in רב הונא's בית דין. The גט was written in שוירי, a town on the river רכיס.
steps.simpleTranslation: For there was a certain גט that was found in the בית דין of רב הונא. Written in it was: 'in the town of שוירי, which is on the river רכיס.' רב הונא said:
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is starting the story that contains the other ruling it mentioned in Step 15. It describes a lost גט that turned up in רב הונא's בית דין, and stops just as רב הונא begins to speak.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The important detail is the place written in the גט: שוירי, on the river רכיס. That detail will matter for the question of whether this גט could belong to a different couple. The ruling itself comes on the next amud.

keyTerms.meaning: A גט, a divorce document.
That was found.
A בית דין, a Jewish court.
The town of שוירי.
The river רכיס.

steps.confusionAlert: This step does not finish. The amud stops at 'רב הונא said:', and his ruling comes on the next amud.

phrases.english: For there was a certain divorce document that was found
in the court of Rav Huna,
in which it was written:
"In the town of Sheviri,
which is on the Rakhis River."
Rav Huna said:

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּהָהוּא גִּיטָּא דְּאִשְׁתְּכַח בֵּי דִינָא דְּרַב הוּנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins the story that contains the second ruling, which the גמרא says would contradict רבה without the rule from Step 14.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: No ruling is given yet. The step only sets up the case: a גט found in רב הונא's בית דין, written in שוירי on the river רכיס.
